question: How should hypernetworks be classified by what conditions them and which target weights they generate, and where do their flexibility and parameter sharing produce genuine advantages or training risks?

key_findings.claim: The review defines a hypernetwork broadly as a network that generates some or all parameters of a target network and classifies designs along five independent axes.
key_findings.evidence: The taxonomy separates hypernetwork input, output generation granularity, target-weight variability, target architecture variability, and hypernetwork architecture, avoiding the common conflation of task conditioning with a particular weight-generation scheme.

key_findings.claim: Output strategy determines the core capacity-efficiency tradeoff: generating all weights is flexible but costly, while chunking, factorization, embeddings, or per-layer generation reduce output burden.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 contrasts generate-once, full, partial, chunked, and other target-weight schemes in terms of output size, sharing, scalability, and compatibility with varying target networks.

key_findings.claim: Applications exploit conditional weight generation for multi-task/personalized models, continual and federated learning, architecture search, domain adaptation, uncertainty, compression, and reinforcement learning.
key_findings.evidence: The application matrix maps conditioning and generation choices to representative results, including task-conditioned policies, data-free rehearsal of prior task weights, domain-specific networks, and heterogeneous-client models.

key_findings.claim: Initialization, scale propagation, memory, output dimensionality, target variability, and limited theory remain central obstacles; a generic hypernetwork can be harder to train than the target it replaces.
key_findings.evidence: The challenges section notes that applying ordinary target-network initialization to the generator does not guarantee correctly scaled generated weights, and that full weight output becomes prohibitive for large targets. The review calls for specialized initialization, efficient generation, stability analysis, and principled architecture design.

method.core_idea: Create a common design vocabulary for hypernetworks by separating conditioning information, generated parameter structure, variability, and network architecture, then use it to organize applications and unresolved problems.
method.mechanism: The narrative review defines hypernetwork and target network roles, constructs tables for input/output/generation variants, surveys application papers by design axes, and synthesizes initialization, scalability, generalization, and theoretical challenges.
assumptions: The selected literature through 2023 covers the main hypernetwork design families despite no systematic-review protocol.
Architecturally different weight-generating systems can be meaningfully compared through the proposed axes.
Reported application gains are attributable in part to conditional weight generation despite heterogeneous baselines.
A broad definition of hypernetwork is more useful than restricting the term to the original full-weight generator.

techniques.role: Distinguishes task, data, noise, embedding, and architecture-conditioned generators.
Compares full, partial, layerwise, chunked, and factored target outputs.
Separates fixed-size targets from variable architectures and populations.
Maps hypernetwork choices to transfer, personalization, continual learning, uncertainty, and RL use cases.

evaluations.setting: Hypernetwork architecture and output-strategy literature through 2023.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative coverage of conditioning, output, variability, and architecture choices.
evaluations.result: The taxonomy captures both original full-weight generators and more scalable chunked/factored/task-conditional variants.
evaluations.baseline: Conventional directly optimized target networks and the original HyperNetworks design.

evaluations.setting: Application survey spanning continual/federated/multi-task learning, domain adaptation, compression, uncertainty, and RL.
evaluations.metric: Reported task performance, parameter sharing, adaptation, or memory benefits in source studies.
evaluations.result: Conditional generation is repeatedly useful where many related target models would otherwise be stored or trained separately, but evidence is not normalized across studies.
evaluations.baseline: Separate per-task networks, shared multi-task networks, and task-specific adaptation baselines in cited work.

evaluations.result: Weight-scale initialization and target-output dimensionality emerge as fundamental issues rather than application-specific details.
evaluations.baseline: Directly initialized and optimized target networks.

limitations: The review is brief and narrative, without documented database search, inclusion criteria, or quantitative meta-analysis.
Fast-moving diffusion, implicit neural representation, and foundation-model hypernetwork work after 2023 is absent.
Application results use incomparable target sizes, parameter budgets, tuning effort, and compute.
The taxonomy does not itself predict which generator design will generalize to unseen conditions.
failure_modes: Naive generator initialization produces target weights at the wrong variance scale and destabilizes signal propagation.
Generating every weight of a large target creates an output bottleneck larger than direct adaptation.
A hypernetwork can memorize task identifiers without learning smooth interpolation to new tasks.
Shared generator capacity can cause interference or catastrophic forgetting across conditions.
reusable_insights: Specify hypernetwork input, output granularity, target variability, and generator architecture independently.
Evaluate unseen-condition interpolation, not only performance on conditioning values seen during training.
Generated-weight distribution should be audited layer by layer against a directly initialized target before training.
open_questions: How can hypernetworks generate or adapt billion-parameter targets without an output-size bottleneck?
Which regularity constraints guarantee smooth behavior between conditioning tasks?
Can specialized initialization and normalization make training as predictable as direct target optimization?

competitive_landscape.title: HyperNetworks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Introduces the modern architecture in which one network generates weights for another.
competitive_landscape.difference: The original paper proposes and evaluates specific recurrent/convolutional generators; this review generalizes the definition and organizes later input/output/application variants.

competitive_landscape.title: Continual Learning with Hypernetworks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses task-conditioned generated weights and output regularization to retain earlier tasks without storing raw replay data.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is a deep application study of one design; the review places continual learning among many motivations and highlights cross-cutting scaling and initialization issues.

competitive_landscape.title: Principled Weight Initialization for Hypernetworks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Directly addresses the generated-weight scale pathology identified as an open problem in the review.
competitive_landscape.difference: It derives and tests specialized initialization rules, providing a concrete solution to one challenge that the survey only diagnoses.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper is the first broad review to classify hypernetworks by design dimensions and synthesize their applications and challenges.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its five-axis taxonomy and application tables place many superficially different weight-generating methods in a common framework.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The main contribution is vocabulary and field organization, not new empirical evidence; the scale and initialization warnings aged particularly well.

reviewer_notes: Read all 19 cached pages including taxonomy and application tables. The original method, a major continual-learning use, and a direct initialization follow-up were checked at primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
